articles.title: In 2007, Sandra Bullock paid $2.725 million for 91 acres near San Diego; she renovated the adobe ranch and built an organic farm with about 1,200 avocado trees before selling the property for $5.6 million
articles.summary: In 2007, Sandra Bullock paid $2.725 million for 91 acres of rolling land in the hills of Valley Center, a rural community northeast of San Diego.
articles.body: In 2007, Sandra Bullock paid $2.725 million for 91 acres of rolling land in the hills of Valley Center, a rural community northeast of San Diego. Over the next decade, she renovated the adobe ranch house, added a guest cottage and barn, and planted an organic farm with roughly 1,200 avocado trees. The property, which she used as a weekend retreat and working farm, sold in 2024 for $5.6 million, according to Mansion Global and Architectural Digest. Read more details about it, as per the reports, here:A quiet ranch in the North County backcountryThe 91-acre ranch sits in Valley Center, an unincorporated area in northern San Diego County known for its open space, equestrian properties and avocado groves. The landscape is defined by rolling hills, oak trees and wide views across the countryside. For Bullock, the property offered a place to escape the pace of Los Angeles and focus on a quieter, more grounded lifestyle. Mansion Global reported that the original home is a Spanish-style adobe ranch built in 1976. When Bullock purchased the land, the house and outbuildings needed significant updates. She set about renovating the main residence, preserving its rustic character while modernising key systems and finishes. The result was a home that felt rooted in the region’s architectural traditions but comfortable for contemporary living.Beyond the house, the property includes a guest cottage, a barn and other outbuildings that support both residential and agricultural use. Those structures allow the ranch to function as a working farm as well as a private retreat. For Bullock, the combination of land, buildings and views created a setting where she could relax, entertain and pursue her interest in sustainable farming.Building an organic avocado farmOne of Bullock’s major investments on the property was the development of an organic avocado farm. She planted about 1,200 avocado trees across the 91 acres, creating one of the larger certified organic groves in the area. The farm is managed as a working agricultural operation, with irrigation systems, access roads and maintenance infrastructure designed to support long-term production.For the unversed, avocado farming in San Diego County is both a tradition and a business. The region’s climate and soil are well suited to the crop, and many local properties combine residential use with small-scale agriculture. By planting a certified organic grove, Bullock aligned the farm with a growing market for sustainably produced food while also maintaining the land in active use rather than leaving it idle.The avocado trees are more than just an investment. They are part of a lifestyle that values connection to the land and the rhythms of growing seasons.For Bullock, who has spoken publicly about her interest in organic food and sustainable living, the farm offered a way to put those values into practice. The grove also adds economic value to the property, as a producing farm can generate income and reduce maintenance costs.Renovations that honoured the original characterThe main house was renovated with an eye toward preserving its original adobe character. Thick walls, exposed beams and traditional materials were preserved wherever possible, but interiors were updated to meet modern standards. The end result is a home that feels authentic to its time and place but is functional for a family that spends weekends and holidays on the ranch, according to Mansion Global. A guest cottage provides additional space for visitors or staff, while a barn and other outbuildings facilitate agricultural operations and storage. These types of buildings are essential to a working farm, allowing for the safe and efficient storage of equipment, supplies and harvested fruit. Together, the buildings create a small compound that can accommodate both residential and farming activities, the report further noted. Landscaping around the home includes native plants, mature trees and open lawns that blend into the surrounding hills. The design prioritizes low water use and compatibility with the local environment, reflecting the same sustainable ethos that guided the avocado farm. For a property of this size, considered landscaping can make a big difference in both esthetics and long-term maintenance.From purchase to saleBullock purchased the ranch in 2007 for $2.725 million, at a time when the San Diego backcountry was still relatively affordable compared to the coastal areas. Over the years she invested in renovations, infrastructure and the avocado grove, turning the property into a fully functioning farm and retreat. The sale for $5.6 million in 2024, according to reports from Architectural Digest and Mansion Global, is a profit of about $2.875 million on the purchase price, but does not include the costs of improvements, farming operations and upkeep. The property was listed through Compass, with agents emphasizing the combination of land, home and working farm. Marketing materials emphasised the 91 acres of rolling terrain, the organic avocado grove, the renovated adobe ranch and the potential for continued agricultural use or private estate living. For buyers interested in a large, self-contained property with both residential and farming potential, the ranch offered a rare opportunity in the San Diego region. The sale comes as Bullock continues to maintain other properties, including homes in Los Angeles and elsewhere in California. The Valley Center ranch was never her primary residence, but rather a weekend and holiday retreat where she could focus on family, friends and the land.Its sale marks the end of that chapter, though the farm itself will continue as a working avocado grove under new ownership.A property that blended lifestyle and agricultureThe Valley Center ranch is an example of how a celebrity property can serve multiple purposes. It was a private escape from public life, a place to host family and friends, and a working farm that produced food and income. That combination is not common in high-profile real estate, where many properties are designed primarily for luxury living rather than agricultural production. For Bullock, the ranch was a way of living more simply and connecting to the land; the avocado grove needed regular care and tending, but it also gave him a tangible connection to the cycles of nature. Those rhythms can be grounding for someone whose professional life is dominated by film schedules, press tours and public appearances. The sale does not diminish the role the property played in her life over nearly two decades. It was a place where she could step away from the spotlight, tend to trees, watch the seasons change and enjoy the quiet of the North County backcountry. For the next owner, the ranch offers a similar opportunity to combine residential living with the rewards and responsibilities of managing a working farm.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.body: NEW DELHI: The news of TMC chairperson Mamata Banerjee arriving in Delhi on Thursday evening has heightened the anticipation that an appointment sought by INDIA bloc for a meeting with President Droupadi Murmu over the functioning of Election Commission and the SIR process may be coming soon.Opposition INDIA bloc parties have agreed to restrict their delegation to 10 as sought by the President Secretariat, sources said.There was no confirmation from opposition parties as of Wednesday night if they have received an appointment from the President’s Secretariat. Opposition has sought time any day between Oct 7-9 from the President and are awaiting a confirmation, sources said.The decision to write over this issue to the President was taken at the INDIA bloc meeting on Sept 30. After that, it is learnt that the bloc wrote seeking time from the President. It was conveyed by the President's secretariat that it would need to restrict their contingent of leaders to not more than 10, sources said.The INDIA bloc has now written back agreeing to the request and they have been asked to restrict their delegation to 10 members, sources said.Meanwhile, even as the Opposition awaits eagerly to hear from the President's secretariat for an appointment, CPI(M)'s Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas shared that his petition, seeking urgent constitutional intervention to safeguard the integrity of the Election Commission, the electoral rolls and the democratic franchise, has been forwarded to the legislative department of the govt.Brittas has received a reply from Rashtrapati Bhawan where it has been highlighted that the legislative department has to look into the petition and communicate the action taken in the matter to the petitioner directly.In his petition dated September 23, Brittas also drew the attention of the President to the pending parliamentary notice in Rajya Sabha seeking the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner.He recalled that a fresh notice was submitted in the Rajya Sabha on 24 April 2026, signed by 73 MPs, invoking the constitutional and statutory provisions governing removal for proved misbehaviour and setting out nine grounds in support of the notice.He has urged that the constitutional process contemplated under Article 324(5) be allowed to proceed without obstruction and that the Government extend the cooperation necessary for Parliament to discharge its constitutional responsibility.Brittas also urged that the President ensure that the union govt's position before the Supreme Court supports effective protection of the franchise, including the annulment of the SIR exercise wherever it is found to be without authority of law or contrary to constitutional safeguards.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Northern lights may return to US and Canada tonight: Where and when to watch the October 8-9 aurora sky show as CME nears Earth and triggers possible G1-G2 geomagnetic storm
articles.summary: The northern lights could put on another show across parts of the United States and Canada this week as a coronal mass ejection (CME) linked to a
articles.body: The northern lights could put on another show across parts of the United States and Canada this week as a coronal mass ejection (CME) linked to a long-duration M1.4 solar flare heads toward Earth.NOAA’s Space Weather Prediction Center has issued a G2 (moderate) geomagnetic storm watch for October 9, forecasting G1 (minor) to G2 conditions as the CME reaches Earth. The eruption originated from active region AR4549 on the Sun on October 6.The forecast could give skywatchers another opportunity to see the aurora borealis, particularly across northern parts of the US and Canada. However, visibility will depend on the strength and timing of the storm, local weather and darkness.CME from M1.4 solar flare heads toward EarthThe solar activity began with a long-duration M1.4-class flare from AR4549 on October 6. NOAA's forecast discussion said the flare was accompanied by a Type II radio sweep and a CME first observed in imagery from the Solar and Heliospheric Observatory.The Solar Influences Data Analysis Center said the CME was detected as a faint, almost full-halo eruption and estimated its projected speed at about 560 kilometres per second. The centre said preliminary analysis indicated an Earth-directed component, with an expected arrival on October 9.NOAA subsequently issued its G2 storm watch, saying G1 to G2 geomagnetic storms were likely on October 9 because of the CME associated with the M1.4 flare.When could the northern lights appear?Current forecasts point to the most promising period being overnight Thursday, October 8, into Friday, October 9.NOAA's forecast indicates geomagnetic activity could begin increasing around 11 p.m. ET Thursday, with conditions potentially reaching G2 levels around 5 a.m. ET Friday.The exact arrival time of a CME can change as scientists receive additional solar-wind observations, so the forecast should be treated as a window rather than a guaranteed schedule.A G1 storm generally favours higher-latitude regions, while a G2 storm can push the auroral oval farther south.Which US states could see the aurora?Under weaker G1 conditions, the best opportunities are expected across Alaska, Canada and the northern tier of the US, including states such as Washington, Idaho, Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, Maine, Vermont and New Hampshire.If geomagnetic activity reaches G2 levels, the aurora could potentially become visible farther south, with forecasts including areas of Oregon, Wyoming, Nebraska, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Colorado, Pennsylvania and New York among the possible viewing regions.The farther south the auroral oval expands, however, the more important darkness and clear skies become.Why does a solar storm create the northern lights?The aurora borealis occurs when charged particles from the Sun interact with Earth's magnetic field and upper atmosphere.As these energetic particles collide with gases in the atmosphere, they transfer energy to atmospheric atoms and molecules. When that energy is released, it produces the glowing colours associated with the northern lights.Green is the most commonly observed colour, although stronger displays can produce red, pink, purple and other hues.Whether those colours are visible from a particular location depends on the storm's strength, the position of the auroral oval, cloud cover, light pollution and the darkness of the sky.How to watch the northern lightsFor anyone hoping to catch the display, the best strategy is to get away from city lights and find a location with a clear view toward the northern horizon.A dark location is especially important because weaker auroras can be difficult to see with the naked eye even when they are present.Skywatchers should also monitor NOAA's real-time aurora forecasts and local weather conditions before heading outside. The forecast can change as the CME approaches and interacts with Earth's magnetic field.The Weather Network also noted that the timing of the predicted storm could favour parts of Canada, although cloud cover will ultimately determine whether observers can see anything.Your smartphone could capture what your eyes missYou do not need professional photography equipment to photograph the aurora.A smartphone's Night Mode can sometimes capture colours that are difficult to distinguish with the naked eye, particularly during weaker geomagnetic storms. A tripod or other stable surface can help because night photography often uses longer exposures.For cameras with manual controls, increasing exposure time and keeping the device steady can improve the chances of recording faint auroral activity.Still, the most important ingredient is location: a dark sky with a clear northern horizon gives observers the best chance of seeing and photographing the show.For the latest conditions, skywatchers should continue checking NOAA's aurora and space-weather forecasts as the October 8-9 CME encounter approaches. The CME's precise arrival and the resulting geomagnetic response remain subject to change.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Who's really played the best thus far through the first half of the college football season?
articles.summary: The Georgia Bulldogs top the SP+ rankings as college football's most efficient team, while Ohio State and Texas rank far differently than the AP Poll.
articles.body: Most agree that the AP Top 25 Poll has become fatally flawed, thanks to a combination of human voter bias, time zone issues, mistakes and the sheer number of games, which makes following each one in detail virtually impossible. These issues start in the preseason polls, which are no more than lightly educated guessing based on recruiting rankings, coaches, the transfer portal, success in the previous season and conference affiliation. Even in season, the polls have become so unreliable and inaccurate that there's a case to be made that they might do more harm than good when the season hits crunch time and the selection committee starts their rankings. One way to solve for this is to look at rankings that are based not on preseason expectations, stadium size, jersey patches, or recruiting rankings, but actual on-field performance. Meaning, how efficient have you been on offense and defense, adjusted for the competition you've faced. What is the success rate you've had on offense, and allowed on defense, again adjusted for the competition you've faced. MIAMI HURRICANES COACH COMES OUT IN FAVOR OF ENDING PRESEASON COLLEGE FOOTBALL POLLS, BLASTS SEC The advantage to this? It filters out noise, like individual game results. Believe it or not, head-to-head matchups don't actually determine which team is better than the other, especially when the teams are closely matched. For example, look at the two games between the Alabama Crimson Tide and Georgia Bulldogs in 2025. In the first matchup, the Tide went into Athens and eked out a 24-21 win. The underlying performance, though, heavily favored Georgia. The Bulldogs averaged 6.7 yards per play, while allowing just 5.2 to Alabama. Georgia averaged a whopping 6.9 yards per rush, while the Tide could only muster 3.1. UGA missed opportunities too, only converting two of their red zone opportunities into points, losing a fumble, and only going 2-8 on third downs and 0-1 on fourth down. As a result, the postgame win expectancy heavily favored Georgia. Per ESPN's SP+, the adjusted scoring margin was Georgia by nearly seven points. The Bulldogs, based on their underlying performance, would win that game nearly 81% of the time. They didn't. Sure enough, when the two teams met again in the SEC Championship, the outcome was very different. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE To say Georgia dominated is a bit of an understatement. Alabama had -3 net rushing yards on 16 tries, a remarkable -0.2 yards per attempt. The third down success rate flipped, with the Tide going 3-14 and Georgia 6-16, plus 2-2 on fourth downs. Despite losing the penalty battle, the Bulldogs rolled, 28-7. The stats backed it up; UGA had 99.8% win expectancy with a +21.2 adjusted scoring margin. Looking at wins and losses is useful and necessary, but often deceiving as to which team is better. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! So what's happened thus far in 2026 that can give us some clues as to who's trending up and who's trending down? The latest SP+ ranking might be a better place to look than the AP Poll for who's truly elite in college football this year. Well, there's one team that somehow seems to have flown a bit under the radar, perhaps due to a lackluster schedule over the first few weeks. Once again, the Georgia Bulldogs are right back at it, with their dominance thus far making them the No. 1 team based on efficiency and success rate, combined with preseason expectations of team quality. Right behind them? Ohio State, a perfect example of on-field results not necessarily matching team quality. The Buckeyes lost to Texas, but the two teams played an essentially equal game, and the Buckeyes' other performances have been more impressive than the Longhorns. So while they've dropped to fifth in the poll, they're a far better team than their ranking suggests. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Speaking of Texas, they're all the way down at No. 8, as once again their offense has looked far less impressive than most expected heading into the season. Meanwhile, the most surprising team? The Nebraska Cornhuskers, who have thoroughly dominated their (easy) schedule through the first half. Don't be stunned though if their game against Indiana is a lot closer than most expect. Despite their win over LSU, Ole Miss hasn't actually been very impressive on the field. The Rebels are No. 9 in the AP Poll, while SP+ has them at No. 35. Mississippi State is No. 27 in SP+ and No. 17 in the poll, inexplicably. Kentucky just dropped out of the top-25, but SP+ has the Wildcats all the way down at No. 45. Other teams, like Iowa and Oklahoma State, are well below their AP number too. These rankings are forward-looking, and will change as the season progresses. But it's a good reminder not to sleep on Georgia, or downplay how good the Buckeyes are, even with the somewhat fluky Texas loss. And another that we don't have to rely on, often not very good, poll voters to figure out which team is more likely to beat another.
